headline: The betting market is well-calibrated: MLB moneyline is essentially efficient, tennis shows only a mild favorite-longshot bias.
method: Proportional devig of the two-way closing price -> implied probability; favorite = max(q, 1-q); bucketed by favorite implied probability, each bucket reports n, mean implied, realized favorite win-rate, the gap, and a 95% Wilson interval -- each row is one independent match/game.

observation_window.note: committed odds corpora (decade-plus per sport), not a rolling cache; pregame closing prices

confounds: proportional devig shifts absolute probability levels vs. other devig methods
closing snapshot only, not a continuous feed
each row is one independent match/game, so binomial Wilson CIs are valid here -- unlike in-game ticks, which are dependent within an event
favorite is defined by closing price, not by any external ranking
bucket boundaries are declared upfront, not tuned to the data
this grades the market's own calibration, not our model -- nothing here is a claim about beating it
